page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v3 is a member of the LASv3 server family, utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes hardware flags for AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_ni, and SVM virtualization.

This instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. For local storage, it bundles 12012 GB of capacity and is Premium Storage capable, making it suitable for data-intensive operations. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the L48as_v3 demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core, ray tracing, and image processing also register in the top 25%. Conversely, memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, single-threaded compression, and database operations on PassMark fall within the average middle 50% range. LLM inference speeds for 135M and 7B models also align with average tier performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of local storage relative to the 48 vCPUs offers a favorable hardware profile for workloads requiring large local scratch space or high-capacity caching without relying solely on external network storage. Given these characteristics, the server is suited for large-scale databases, data warehousing, multi-threaded data processing, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
